content: 1. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the absorption of gemifloxacin in the gastrointestinal tract, leading to decreased drug levels. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. To minimize this effect, administer gemifloxacin and magnesium hydroxide at least 2 hours apart. Monitor the patient closely. 2. Magnesium oxide also decreases gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both drugs. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor the patient for therapeutic efficacy. 3. Magnesium sulfate reduces gemifloxacin levels by interfering with gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Administer the two agents at least 2 hours apart and monitor the patient closely. 4. Magnesium supplements can form insoluble complexes with gemifloxacin, reducing its absorption in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer magnesium 2 hours before or 3 hours after gemifloxacin to avoid this interaction. Monitor therapy closely. 5. Gemifloxacin and maprotiline both prolong the QTc interval. Use these drugs with caution and monitor the patient for signs of QTc prolongation. 6. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and meclofenamate increases the risk of central nervous system (CNS) stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Modify therapy as needed and monitor the patient closely. 7. Gemifloxacin and mefenamic acid also increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures when used together. Adjust therapy and monitor the patient carefully. 8. Gemifloxacin and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient for potential cardiac effects. 9. Gemifloxacin and meloxicam increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures when used together. Modify therapy and monitor the patient closely. 10. Gemifloxacin may reduce the effectiveness of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Gemifloxacin enhances the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor for potential dysglycemia, as quinolone antibiotics can cause hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. Gatifloxacin is most likely to cause dysglycemia, while moxifloxacin is least likely. 12. Co-administration of methylprednisolone and gemifloxacin increases the risk of tendon rupture due to the combined effects of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 13. Gemifloxacin and mifepristone both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy if possible, and monitor the patient closely. Consider alternative treatments if available. 14. Gemifloxacin enhances the effects of miglitol through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor for dysglycemia, as quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. 15. Gemifloxacin and mirtazapine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient for potential cardiac effects. 16. Use caution and monitor the patient for potential cardiac effects. 22. Gemifloxacin and olanzapine both prolong the QTc interval. Limited data suggest that olanzapine may rarely cause significant QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 23. Gemifloxacin and olodaterol (inhaled) both prolong the QTc interval. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may potentiate the cardiovascular effects of beta-2 agonists, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 24. Gemifloxacin and osilodrostat both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient for potential cardiac effects. 25. Gemifloxacin and osimertinib both prolong the QTc interval. Conduct periodic ECG and electrolyte monitoring in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QTc interval. 26. Oxaliplatin increases gemifloxacin levels or effects through an unknown mechanism. Gemifloxacin and oxaprozin increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures when used together. Modify therapy and monitor the patient closely. 28.
